newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua says reviews coffee production estimates.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua says reviews coffee production estimates.

text.p: Nicaragua's coffee chief said Wednesday officials are reviewing upcoming coffee cycle production estimates and will likely lower them.

David Robleto, president of the National Union of Coffee Producers, told Reuters Nicaragua will likely produce about one million quintales (46-kg) of coffee in 1996-97, of which it will export between 800,000 and 850,000 quintales.
Preliminary projections in early August had put Nicaragua's coffee production at 1,071,649 quintales.
These estimates are a significant drop from the 1995-96 coffee cycle when Nicaragua produced 1,200,917 quintales of coffee and exported 1,116,760 quintales.
Robleto said Nicaragua's October 20 presidential election will affect the 1996-97 coffee crop.
"This is an election year and this has reduced the economic attention the government has given to agricultural production," he said.
Robleto said with the army and police protecting the election process, they are providing less protection for coffee producers who are being hurt by a theft.
